newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher for 5th straight session.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher for 5th straight session.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher, but off early highs, on Friday for the fifth straight day of rebounds as electronics emerged again to lead the upswing, brokers said.
The index ended up 24.96 points or 0.29 percent at 8,654.19, off from an intraday high of 8,716.41.
Turnover was a brisk T$159.5 billion.
Electronics, which fell on Thursday, surged 2.74 percent, with chipmaker United Microelectronics up T$1 to T$68.5 and Taiwan Semiconductor up T$1.5 to T$89.5.
"Investors, even institutional investors, still believe the electronics sector is the best choice despite its recent rallies," said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin.
But some brokers were cautious about recent rallies.
"Recent index rises have relied too much on electronics, which are overheated despite their sound profit outlook," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.
Food shares rebounded 2.45 percent after farm officials late on Thursday said a suspected outbreak of a deadly chicken epidemic was only a false alarm.
Electrical and plastic shares also rose.

Polyester yarn shares surged as makers decided to raise partially oriented yarn and polyester drawn texturised yarn prices in May. Hong Yi Fiber rose by the daily seven percent limit to T$52.5, brokers said.
Brokers said the yarn price hikes reflect the rising demand triggered by the recovering domestic economy.
"The price hikes reflect the recoverying economy, so related share prices have the potential to rise some 15 percent in the next three months," said Michael Hung, an independent analyst.
But financial shares, which led Thursday's gains, fell 1.02 percent, with First Commercial Bank down T$4 to T$120.
Several brokers said a six-year resistance level at about 8,700 remained strong and would be hard to break through in the near term.
But Lin of Golden Securities was more optimistic.
"Unless the government takes moves to cool off the market, the index, I believe, still likely will move gradually firmer to test 8,900 in the near term," Lin said.
